facts.fact_text: On 18 November 2003 at around 10.50 a.m. a group of twenty-three individuals, including the applicants, entered the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse in Istanbul.
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "End the Isolation" ("Tecride Son").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "No to invasion" ("İşgale Hayır").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "Close İmralı Prison" ("İmralı Cezaevi Kapatılsın").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "We have not surrendered and we will not surrender" ("Teslim olmadık olmayacağız").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "Salute, salute a thousand salutes to İmralı" ("Selam, Selam, İmralıya Bin Selam").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "Freedom to Öcalan" ("Öcalan'a Özgürlük").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "The messenger of peace is in İmralı" ("Barış elçisi İmralı'da").
Members of the group hung a large banner from one of the windows of the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse.
Members of the group threw leaflets outside from the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse.
The banner read: "A democratic solution to the Kurdish problem; İmralı Prison must be shut down" ("Kürt sorununa demokratik çözüm, İmralı Cezaevi kapatılsın").
The banner also read: "Youth Initiative for Social Peace" ("Toplumsal Barış için Gençlik Girişimi").
The leaflets thrown from the corridor contained critical remarks concerning the policies of the governing Justice and Development Party.

The applicants later submitted to the Istanbul Assize Court (the trial court) that they had originally planned to make a press statement in front of the Sultanahmet Courthouse, but that they had entered the building owing to the rain.

The applicants submitted to the Istanbul Assize Court (the trial court) that they had attempted to go outside again to make the press statement, but that certain civilians had attacked them with a view to lynching them, forcing them to seek shelter in the closest corridor.

According to witness statements, the protesters warned other individuals present in the corridor and inside the offices that they were going to stage a protest but that there was no need to be afraid.
Witnesses mainly reported hearing repetitive slogans being chanted outside in the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse.
Witnesses reported that they had come to no harm during the protest.
The protesters, including the applicants, continued their actions for about an hour until the police broke in and arrested them.
The applicants mainly stated to the public prosecutor on 22 November 2003 that they had agreed to take part in a peaceful protest concerning the "Kurdish problem".
The rest of the applicants stated at the hearing on 19 April 2004 that they had planned to peacefully make a press statement in front of the Sultanahmet Courthouse.

At the hearing on 19 April 2004, the applicants' lawyers submitted to the Istanbul Assize Court (the trial court) that the incident had in fact comprised no more than the making of a simple press statement.
At the end of the questioning on 22 November 2003, the judge of the Istanbul State Security Court placed all the applicants in pre-trial detention.
On 10 December 2003 the Istanbul public prosecutor filed a bill of indictment against the applicants.
The Istanbul public prosecutor charged the applicant Ekrem Can with membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 168 of the former Criminal Code.
The Istanbul public prosecutor charged the applicant Fikret Avras with membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 168 of the former Criminal Code.
The Istanbul public prosecutor charged the applicant Mahmut Cengiz with membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 168 of the former Criminal Code.
The Istanbul public prosecutor charged the applicant Şenol Akyaz with membership of a terrorist organisation under Article 168 of the former Criminal Code.

The Istanbul public prosecutor charged the applicants Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras, Mahmut Cengiz and Şenol Akyaz with possessing and using explosive materials under Article 264 § 6 in fine of the former Criminal Code.

The Istanbul public prosecutor charged the rest of the applicants (other than Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras, Mahmut Cengiz and Şenol Akyaz) with aiding and abetting a terrorist organisation under Article 169 of the former Criminal Code.

The Istanbul public prosecutor charged all the applicants with "interrupting public services through coercion, distortion or the commission of unlawful acts" under Article 188 § 5 in fine of the former Criminal Code.
On 26 December 2006 the Istanbul Assize Court delivered its judgment in the case.

The Istanbul Assize Court found that the applicants had chanted certain slogans, waved a banner from the windows, and closed the door to the corridor, preventing officials from entering by placing metal cupboards behind the door to form a barricade, thereby trapping the lawyers and the court personnel and hampering them in the performance of their duties.
The Istanbul Assize Court found all the applicants guilty under Article 113 § 1 of the Criminal Code of "interrupting public services through coercion, distortion or the commission of unlawful acts".
The Istanbul Assize Court sentenced each of the applicants to one year and eight months' imprisonment under Article 113 § 1 of the Criminal Code.

The Istanbul Assize Court found all the applicants, except for Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras, Mahmut Cengiz and Şenol Akyaz, guilty under Article 169 of the former Criminal Code of aiding and abetting an armed gang.
The Istanbul Assize Court sentenced each of the applicants convicted under Article 169 of the former Criminal Code to three years and nine months' imprisonment.

The Istanbul Assize Court found the applicants Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras, Mahmut Cengiz and Şenol Akyaz guilty of membership of an armed terrorist organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code.
The Istanbul Assize Court sentenced the applicants Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras, Mahmut Cengiz and Şenol Akyaz each to six years and three months' imprisonment under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code.
On 18 March 2009, following an appeal by the applicants, the Court of Cassation partially upheld and partially quashed the Istanbul Assize Court's judgment.
The Court of Cassation upheld the convictions of the applicants Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras, Mahmut Cengiz and Şenol Akyaz under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code.
The Court of Cassation upheld the convictions of the applicants Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras and Mahmut Cengiz under Article 174 § 1 of the Criminal Code.
The Court of Cassation upheld the convictions of the rest of the applicants under Article 169 of the former Criminal Code.
The Court of Cassation quashed the convictions of all the applicants under Article 113 § 1 of the Criminal Code.
The Court of Cassation quashed the convictions of the applicants Ekrem Can, Fikret Avras and Mahmut Cengiz for using explosive materials under Article 170 § 1 (c) of the Criminal Code.
On 30 June 2010 the Istanbul Assize Court once again convicted all the applicants under Article 113 § 1 of the Criminal Code.
On 30 June 2010 the Istanbul Assize Court sentenced each of the applicants to one year and eight months' imprisonment under Article 113 § 1 of the Criminal Code.
On 30 June 2010 the Istanbul Assize Court convicted the applicant Ekrem Can on two counts of using explosive materials under Article 170 § 1 (c) of the Criminal Code.
On 30 June 2010 the Istanbul Assize Court sentenced the applicant Ekrem Can to ten months' imprisonment under Article 170 § 1 (c) of the Criminal Code for using explosive materials.

On 30 June 2010 the Istanbul Assize Court sentenced the applicant Mahmut Cengiz to five months' imprisonment under Article 170 § 1 (c) of the Criminal Code for throwing Molotov cocktails.

Witness M.A.İ. stated that he had been waiting his turn to attend a hearing before a court at the Sultanahmet Courthouse when a noisy quarrel had broken out in the corridor.
Witness M.A.İ. stated that after the clamour in the corridor had escalated, the judge had discontinued the hearing.
Witness M.A.İ. stated that the people in the hearing room had moved some cabinets behind the hearing room's door in order to securely block the entrance.
Witness M.A.İ. stated that he and others had been confined in the hearing room for a further forty-five minutes.
Witness M.A.İ. stated that the tear gas used to disperse the group had affected the people in the hearing room.
Witness M.A.İ. stated that the judge had postponed the rest of the proceedings scheduled for that day as a result of the incident.

Witness G.İ., a clerk working for a court at the Sultanahmet Courthouse, attested that at around 10 a.m. on 18 November 2003 two individuals had come into the registry of that court, stating that they would give a statement in the corridor and would not harm anyone.
Witness G.İ. stated that the group had first chanted PKK-related slogans and the name of Abdullah Öcalan.
Witness G.İ. stated that she and the other people who had barricaded themselves into the hearing room had then unblocked the door and left the office after about an hour.
Witness G.İ. stated that she had not identified any damage in the corridor after the incident.
